Maladaptive Strategies.value: I imagine getting revenge on the people responsible
constantly check body for signs of danger or injury
I detach myself from the memories

Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I feel on guard even inside my own home

Memory.value: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.

Negative Appraisals.value: I acted in ways that go against who I am
Somebody else would have stopped the event from happening

vignette: Kofi's life as a young chef was one of creativity and precision, but it all changed on a night that still feels like yesterday. He had been walking home from work when he was ambushed by a group of men who subjected him to a brutal sexual assault. The violence and sense of utter helplessness left an indelible mark on Kofi's psyche. As time passed, Kofi found himself increasingly on edge whenever he encountered triggers that transported him back to that fateful night. Car sounds, which had once been a familiar background hum, now made his heart skip a beat, reminding him of the screeching tires and revving engines of his attackers' getaway cars. The memory of being overpowered also left Kofi with an intense fear of losing control - in the kitchen, on the streets, or even in his own home. These triggers sent Kofi's mind racing into dark territories, where he would fantasize about revenge against those who had wronged him. He'd imagine himself overpowering them, regaining control and dominance. But these fantasies only seemed to fuel a sense of perpetual threat. False alarms became a regular occurrence - every sudden movement by a stranger on the street or an unexpected noise at home would put Kofi immediately on guard, his body tensed for battle. Even in his own kitchen, where he once felt safest, he'd find himself constantly checking his surroundings, monitoring his body for signs of danger or injury. These hypervigilant behaviors only seemed to intensify the threat, as if by being always "on," Kofi might prevent another assault. However, this constant state of alertness couldn't shield him from the memories that haunted him. Triggers like car sounds would instantly bring back the full, unvarnished memory of that night without warning, complete with the auditory recall of his attackers' jeers and the screeching tires. But when Kofi tried to explain what had happened to himself or others, he'd become mired in a quagmire of self-doubt, unable to articulate the events clearly. Kofi's inability to shake these memories and triggers only served to reinforce his negative appraisals of himself. He believed that he had acted in ways that went against who he was - that he should have fought back harder, been stronger. This conviction fueled a sense of hopelessness; Kofi felt as though he had no future worth fighting for, that the assault had irreparably damaged him. This toxic cycle of negative self-appraisal further entrenched Kofi's maladaptive strategies. The more he fantasized about revenge or detached himself from his memories, the more those memories seemed to surface, threatening to overwhelm him at any moment. Conversely, the more Kofi tried to explain what had happened - only to falter and fail - the more convinced he became that others would have coped better in his shoes. As this self-reinforcing cycle tightened its grip on Kofi's psyche, he found himself increasingly isolated from friends, family, and even his passion for cooking. He was trapped in a living nightmare of triggers, threats, memories, and maladaptive coping strategies - a vicious loop that seemed to have no escape. It was only when this desperate feeling finally became too much to bear that Kofi sought help, hoping against hope that therapy might offer him a way out of the darkness that had consumed his life.
